concepts.def: How well a protein source matches body needs.
High biological value, e.g. eggs, milk, soya.

Speed a carb raises blood glucose levels.
Essential unsaturated fatty acid in oily fish.

walkthroughs.body_html: A protein's biological value describes how completely it matches our amino acid needs. HBV proteins like egg and soya tick every box. LBV proteins like wheat lack one or more essentials and need combining.

The glycaemic index ranks how fast a carb raises blood glucose. Low-GI foods like porridge release energy slowly. Dietary fibre — found in wholegrains, fruit, vegetables — slows digestion further and supports gut health. UK adults are advised about 30 g fibre a day.

The body cannot make omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, so they must come from food. Oily fish like salmon and mackerel are top sources of omega-3, supporting brain and heart health. Government advice is two portions of fish per week, one oily.
